claims.text: The paper provides a systematic analysis of multi-modal multi-task visual understanding foundation models (MM-VUFMs) designed specifically for road scenes.
MM-VUFMs process and fuse data from diverse modalities in driving contexts.
MM-VUFMs simultaneously handle various driving-related visual tasks.

evidence.description: The authors survey task-specific models, unified multi-modal models, unified multi-task models, and prompting techniques across learning paradigms for road scene understanding.
The survey documents model architectures that combine multi-modal inputs for visual scene perception in intelligent vehicles.
The paper categorizes multi-task foundation models capable of performing concurrent driving-related vision objectives.

methodologies.name: Systematic Literature Survey and Taxonomy
methodologies.description: A comprehensive analysis and taxonomy of multi-modal multi-task visual understanding foundation models across architectures, learning paradigms, and application challenges in road scenes.

limitations.text: Existing MM-VUFMs struggle with interpretability, deployment under low-resource conditions, and integration into closed-loop driving systems.

future_work.text: Development of closed-loop driving systems integrated with MM-VUFMs.
Enhancing the interpretability of MM-VUFMs in autonomous driving applications.
Optimizing MM-VUFMs for operation under low-resource conditions.
Investigating embodied driving agents and world models in conjunction with foundation models.
